![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The PR description mentions adding a required `Purpose / Why / Info flow` comment block to the file header, but it is currently missing from the file.

```suggestion
<!--
Purpose: Define the design system tokens and prose for Meechie's Playful Canvas.
Why: Align implementation with design tokens and maintain consistency.
Info flow: design.md -> +layout.svelte / CSS variables.
-->
---
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The color tokens in the YAML block do not match the updated colors described in the PR description (e.g., fuchsia primary, gold secondary, etc.).

```suggestion
colors:
  primary: "#e8006a"
  secondary: "#c9a227"
  tertiary: "#f0c44a"
  neutral-light: "#fdf6e3"
  neutral-dark: "#07070f"
  accent-success: "#00c896"
  accent-joy: "#b8aacf"
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The typography tokens still use `system-ui` and the label font size is still `14px`, which contradicts the PR description's claim of using loaded fonts (Fraunces, Bricolage Grotesque, Barlow Condensed) and raising the label font size to `16px`.

```markdown
typography:
  h1:
    fontFamily: Fraunces, serif
    fontSize: 48px
    fontWeight: 700
    lineHeight: 1.2
    letterSpacing: -0.02em
  h2:
    fontFamily: Fraunces, serif
    fontSize: 36px
    fontWeight: 600
    lineHeight: 1.3
  body-lg:
    fontFamily: Bricolage Grotesque, sans-serif
    fontSize: 18px
    fontWeight: 400
    lineHeight: 1.6
  body-md:
    fontFamily: Bricolage Grotesque, sans-serif
    fontSize: 16px
    fontWeight: 400
    lineHeight: 1.5
  label:
    fontFamily: Barlow Condensed, sans-serif
    fontSize: 16px
    fontWeight: 600
    lineHeight: 1.4
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The components block is missing `button-tertiary` and the `input` token is missing `borderWidth` and `focusBorderColor` properties as described in the PR description.

```markdown
components:
  button-primary:
    backgroundColor: "{colors.primary}"
    textColor: "#FFFFFF"
    rounded: "{rounded.lg}"
    padding: "12px 24px"
  button-secondary:
    backgroundColor: "{colors.secondary}"
    textColor: "#FFFFFF"
    rounded: "{rounded.lg}"
    padding: "12px 24px"
  button-tertiary:
    backgroundColor: "transparent"
    borderColor: "{colors.tertiary}"
    textColor: "{colors.tertiary}"
    borderWidth: "1px"
    rounded: "{rounded.lg}"
    padding: "12px 24px"
  card:
    backgroundColor: "#FFFFFF"
    rounded: "{rounded.lg}"
    padding: "24px"
    boxShadow: "0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.08)"
  input:
    backgroundColor: "#F9F9F9"
    borderColor: "#E0E0E0"
    borderWidth: "1px"
    focusBorderColor: "{colors.primary}"
    rounded: "{rounded.md}"
    padding: "12px 16px"
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The color descriptions in the prose section still refer to the old color names and hex codes instead of the updated color palette.

```suggestion
- **Primary (#e8006a):** Fuchsia primary that signals joy and creativity. Used for primary actions and interactive highlights.
- **Secondary (#c9a227):** Gold secondary for secondary actions and informational content. Creates contrast while remaining calm.
- **Tertiary (#f0c44a):** Bright tertiary for accents and micro-interactions that delight without overwhelming.
- **Neutral Light (#fdf6e3):** Cream neutral-light background that reduces eye strain and feels paper-like (echoing the coloring book metaphor).
- **Neutral Dark (#07070f):** Neutral-dark for text and structural elements, maintaining high readability.
- **Success (#00c896):** Emerald success for positive feedback, celebrations, and completion states.
- **Joy (#b8aacf):** Lavender joy for highlights and moments of celebration.
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The max-width in prose is still `1200px` instead of `1240px` as described in the PR description.

```suggestion
Content flows in a single-column layout on mobile with optional multi-column grids on desktop (max 1240px). The 8px spacing scale provides rhythm and breathing room. Generous padding (24px container padding) makes the interface feel open and non-cramped.
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The input border-radius in prose is still `4px` instead of `8px` as described in the PR description.

```suggestion
All interactive elements use rounded corners (8px on inputs, 12px on buttons and cards) to feel approachable and less clinical. Consistency across shapes reinforces the playful aesthetic.
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The PR description mentions removing the `as never` cast since `promptCompilerInputFixture` is already of type `PromptCompilerInput`, but the cast is still present in the code.

```suggestion
    const compiled = await seam.compile(promptCompilerInputFixture);
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The PR description states that `galleryRecordFaultFixture` is exported as `unknown` so that no cast is needed at test sites. However, it is currently cast to `GalleryRecord` using `as unknown as GalleryRecord`. It should be cast simply to `as unknown`.

```suggestion
export const galleryRecordFaultFixture = {
  id: '',
  createdAt: '',
  request: promptCompilerInputFixture,
  compiled: compiledPromptFixture,
  images: []
} as unknown;
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The PR description states that fault fixtures are exported as `unknown`. However, `promptCompilerInputFaultFixture` is currently cast to `PromptCompilerInput` using `as unknown as PromptCompilerInput`.

```suggestion
export const promptCompilerInputFaultFixture = {
  description: '',
  glamLevel: 6,
  density: 'medium',
  lineThickness: 'medium',
  borderStyle: 'none',
  addCaption: false
} as unknown;
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Defer the cast of `compiledPromptFaultFixture` to `CompiledPrompt` here at the usage site, as described in the PR description.

```suggestion
export const getCompiledPromptFixture = (scenario: 'sample' | 'fault' = 'sample'): CompiledPrompt =>
  scenario === 'fault' ? (compiledPromptFaultFixture as CompiledPrompt) : compiledPromptFixture;
```

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add the required top-level file header**

This new file starts directly with YAML front matter, but the repo-level `AGENTS.md` requires every file to start with a top-level comment describing what it does, why it does it, and how information flows. As added, `design.md` violates that documented repository standard, so the next governance/checklist review will have no required purpose/why/info-flow header to verify.
